construction.access_recipe: For each fiscal year fy in 2008..2023 (sixteen archives; FY2007 is outside the frozen population window) fetch https://reporter.nih.gov/exporter/projects/download/{fy}, open the largest CSV member of the ZIP, and read it as all-string dtypes in bounded chunks. Normalize headers to the documented uppercase names (APPLICATION_TYPE, ACTIVITY, ADMINISTERING_IC, CORE_PROJECT_NUM, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE, BUDGET_START, PROJECT_START, TOTAL_COST, DIRECT_COST_AMT, INDIRECT_COST_AMT, ORG_NAME, ORG_STATE, ORG_COUNTRY, ORG_IPF_CODE, ED_INST_TYPE, STUDY_SECTION, PI_IDS, SUPPORT_YEAR, FY) and record which solicitation header names each file exposes; OPPORTUNITY_NUMBER (the FOA number) is present in every audited year and is surveyed but not shipped under the frozen twelve-column feature contract. Parse dates as YYYY-MM-DD, coercing errors to null, and treat empty strings as missing rather than zero. Keep only ACTIVITY code R01 with APPLICATION_TYPE code 1 and SUPPORT_YEAR code 1 and non-missing PROJECT_START, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and ORG_STATE as candidate first-year rows; keep one row per CORE_PROJECT_NUM. Build the label by self-joining on CORE_PROJECT_NUM: any APPLICATION_TYPE 2 record with BUDGET_START strictly after the row PROJECT_START and no later than PROJECT_START plus six years gives a positive; drop rows whose six-year window extends past the FY2023 cutoff instead of labeling them negative. Compute PI histories by sorting on AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and using only strictly earlier records, never PROJECT_END. Count application types and activity codes by prefix so excluded populations are evidenced without aborting, and measure direct and indirect cost blanks per fiscal-year cohort instead of assuming the published FY2012-onward availability note describes the current files.
construction.expected_size: 17 archives at the published sizes of roughly 39-68 MB each (about 0.9 GB of compressed download); uncompressed CSV files are several times larger, and a recent fiscal-year project file holds on the order of 10^5 award-support-year records (explicitly estimated; confirm on first read). New R01 type-1 rows are a small slice, estimated at a few thousand per cohort year, giving roughly 30-60k population rows across FY2008-FY2017.
construction.format: One ZIP archive per fiscal year, each containing a single comma-delimited CSV with a header row and one record per award-support-year (so a multi-year project contributes one record per fiscal year with increasing SUPPORT_YEAR).
construction.source_examples: Documented and checkable on first read: ACTIVITY values include 'R01', 'R21', 'P01'; APPLICATION_TYPE values '1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '7', '9'; SUPPORT_YEAR increments 1,2,3... within a core project number; ORG_STATE holds two-letter state codes and ORG_COUNTRY holds country names; FY is a four-digit fiscal year; award notice and budget start dates are ISO-style dates. Cost columns exist but are blank before FY2012, which is a documented cohort-dependent missingness pattern.

evidence.claim: APPLICATION_TYPE is a documented one-digit code distinguishing new applications from competing continuations, which is what makes the renewal label computable.
CORE_PROJECT_NUM is the project-level identifier that persists across award years, enabling continuity tracking without hand matching.
evidence.quote: This identifier is not specific to any particular year of the project.

evidence.claim: PROJECT_END is extended when a competing renewal is awarded, so it encodes future outcome information and must not be used as a feature.
evidence.quote: Upon competitive renewal of a grant, the project end date is extended by the length of the renewal award.

evidence.claim: Documented review-panel and organization-type fields support non-text, award-time features.
evidence.quote: A designator of the legislatively-mandated panel of subject matter experts that reviewed the research grant application for scientific and technical merit.

evidence.claim: Bulk project files are downloadable by fiscal year from a documented URL pattern, with no account or API key.
Files are plain CSV extracts of public RePORTER data, sized in the tens of megabytes per fiscal year, which makes a multi-cohort build tractable on a small worker.
evidence.quote: ExPORTER provides bulk administrative data found in RePORTER to the public for detailed analyses or to load into their own data systems.

evidence.claim: Statutory basis: U.S. government works of this kind are not subject to copyright in the United States, so reuse does not depend on a publisher licence grant.
evidence.quote: The effect of section 105 is intended to place all works of the United States Government, published or unpublished, in the public domain.

evidence.claim: Scope of that basis: the exemption reaches works prepared by government officers or employees in the course of official duties, which describes these agency-compiled award records.
evidence.quote: a work prepared by an officer or employee of the United States Government as part of that person's official duties

limitations: Retrospective snapshot, not a historical operational feed: each annual file reflects the administrative state of the records when that file was created, so later revisions (amount changes, no-cost extensions, PI moves) appear in the vintage you download; this demonstrates that the outcome is documented, not that an analyst could have queried these exact rows on the notice date.

PROJECT_END is excluded from features because NIH extends it on renewal; TOTAL_COST may also be administratively revised, so amounts are treated as award-time values rather than audited first-year outlays.

The outcome is partly behavioral: a renewal exists only if the investigator applied, so the label measures continuation of federal funding rather than scientific merit alone, and it co-moves with appropriations and institute paylines across fiscal years.

Correlated observations: prolific investigators and large institutions contribute many rows, so rows are not independent draws; cluster-aware evaluation by PI and institution is advisable and the identity baselines must be reported.
PI_ID values are not perfectly stable (accounts split or merge over time; contract and subproject cases are known to vary), so PI histories carry linkage noise.
Direct and indirect cost fields are only populated from FY2012 onward, creating systematic missingness for the earliest training cohorts.
Legal basis is U.S. law and territorial: 17 U.S.C. 105 removes U.S. copyright in these agency-compiled records; it is not a worldwide dedication, and no foreign rights are asserted or waived.

Grantee-supplied text (abstracts, public health relevance statements, project titles) may carry third-party rights and is excluded: it is neither used as a feature nor redistributed. The derived release is award-level administrative metadata only, with PI identifiers pseudonymized.
Only linked via the same agency's own files (project and, if used, PI/organization lookups); no external registry, credit, or personal data is joined.
reason: NIH RePORTER/ExPORTER bulk award files are a no-account, no-join, directly downloadable federal dataset (one CSV per fiscal year, ~39-68 MB each) with a published field dictionary and a binary forward outcome that is computable from documented fields: whether a newly awarded R01 project later receives a competing-renewal (type 2) award on the same core project number. Reuse rests on a statutory public-domain basis (17 U.S.C. 105, works prepared by U.S. government officers/employees in the course of official duties) rather than a publisher licence grant, the data are award-level (institutional, not sensitive personal information), and ten annual cohorts of new R01s supply several thousand independent decision rows per year with a roughly balanced label. Two documented pitfalls are handled explicitly in the design: PROJECT_END is contaminated by later renewals and is excluded, and all historical/identity features are computed only from records dated strictly before each row's decision instant.

task.decision_user: A principal investigator's lab manager or a research development office deciding, at the notice of award, whether to plan and budget for a competing-renewal submission and a possible funding gap.

features.availability: Printed on the first-year award record at notice; current snapshot supports field meaning but does not prove historical first-year availability.
features.meaning: Two-character NIH institute or center code administering the award; captures institute-specific continuation norms and paylines.
features.name: administering_ic

features.availability: Review panel field recorded with the award; current snapshot supports field meaning but does not prove historical first-year availability.
features.meaning: Review panel code that evaluated the funded application; proxies field and review culture. The panel name text is not shipped to avoid duplicate text.
features.name: study_section

features.availability: Printed on the first-year award record at notice; current snapshot supports field meaning but does not prove historical first-year availability.
features.meaning: NIH grouping of the grantee organization component type, such as medical school, other college, hospital or business.
features.name: ed_inst_type

features.availability: Printed on the first-year award record at notice and required non-missing for population eligibility; historical availability assumed.
features.meaning: Two-letter grantee business-office state; institutional location and clustering. Required non-missing for population eligibility.
features.name: org_state

features.availability: Printed on the first-year award record at notice; historical availability assumed.
features.meaning: Grantee business-office country; institutional location and foreign or domestic status.
features.name: org_country

features.availability: Printed on the first-year award record at notice; high-cardinality institution identifier; historical availability assumed.
features.meaning: Stable NIH institution identifier for the grantee organization; institutional capacity and high-cardinality identity control.
features.name: org_ipf_code

features.availability: Printed on the first-year award record at notice; later administrative revisions are possible, so treated as award-time value.
features.meaning: First-year total award amount, direct plus indirect; treated as an award-time value because later administrative revisions are possible.
features.name: total_cost

features.availability: Measured in this vintage as populated on the released first-year records, including the pre-FY2012 cohorts; the published FY2012-onward note in the NIH dictionary describes an earlier snapshot of the file contents. Blank remains missing, not zero.
features.meaning: First-year direct cost component; indirect share proxies institutional facilities and administrative rate.
features.name: direct_cost_amt

features.availability: Measured in this vintage as populated on the released first-year records, including the pre-FY2012 cohorts, with only a handful of blank rows; the published FY2012-onward note in the NIH dictionary describes an earlier snapshot of the file contents. Blank remains missing, not zero. Award-level amounts are near-unique, so the column is declared high-cardinality.
features.meaning: First-year indirect cost component; proxies institutional facilities and administrative rate.
features.name: indirect_cost_amt

features.availability: Derived from PROJECT_START printed on the first-year award record.
features.meaning: Calendar month of PROJECT_START, giving within-year timing while remaining visible at notice.
features.name: project_start_month

features.availability: Derived from the PI identifier list printed on the first-year award record; a missing list remains missing.
features.meaning: Number of distinct PI identifiers on the first-year record; single-PI versus multi-PI structure.
features.name: multi_pi_count

features.availability: Uses only records with AWARD_NOTICE_DATE strictly earlier than the row notice date; a missing PI identifier list remains missing; left-censored before the first downloaded annual file.
features.meaning: Maximum number of distinct earlier R01 core projects held by any listed PI, measuring established versus first-time R01 holders without using labels.
features.name: pi_prior_r01_count

task.outcome_horizon: 6 years from the initial PROJECT_START (typical R01 project periods are 3-5 years, so the first competing renewal normally begins in year 4-6); cohorts through FY2017 are fully observed using files through FY2023.
task.population: Extramural R01 awards in the annual NIH ExPORTER project files with APPLICATION_TYPE code 1 (new), SUPPORT_YEAR code 1, ACTIVITY code R01, non-missing PROJECT_START, AWARD_NOTICE_DATE and ORG_STATE, and AWARD_NOTICE_DATE from 2007-10-01 through 2017-09-30 (federal fiscal years 2008-2017). The released splits ship fiscal years 2008-2012 to train, 2013-2014 to eval, and 2015-2016 to holdout; the FY2017 cohort is held back outside the three release files as a post-holdout drift audit. Excludes other application types, contracts with N-prefix codes, intramural Z-prefix codes, and projects whose first-year record is missing. Eligibility uses only fields visible on the award record at the decision instant.
task.prediction_time: The award notice date (AWARD_NOTICE_DATE) printed on the project first-year record, the moment the new award becomes public. Features use only fields printed on that first-year record or histories built from R01 award records with AWARD_NOTICE_DATE strictly earlier than the row notice date.
task.question: When NIH announces a brand-new R01 award, will that project later be continued through a competing-renewal award on the same core project number, or will the project end without one?
task.simple_references: Persistence/majority baseline: each fiscal-year cohort renewal rate, constant per split. Calendar baseline: fiscal-year cohort and project start month. Identity baseline: organization identifier ORG_IPF_CODE and administering institute/review panel. No persistence score column exists in the source; the identity reference uses only shipped entity columns and training-only calendar rates.
task.split_policy: One row per new award; assignment by AWARD_NOTICE_DATE with hard fiscal-year boundaries (Oct 1 - Sep 30) and no shuffling: train FY2008-FY2012, eval FY2013-FY2014, holdout FY2015-FY2016; FY2017 is held back as a post-holdout drift check and never used for tuning. No calendar embargo gap is imposed, because every feature for a row is restricted to records dated strictly before that row's notice date, and every label uses only post-decision records of that same core project; instead right-censoring is enforced by requiring the full 6-year window to be observed at the data cutoff. Identity/aggregate features additionally obey the rule that they may use only cohorts whose outcome window closed before the decision instant, so a later row can never disclose an earlier row's target.
task.target: y = 1 if the same CORE_PROJECT_NUM has any award record with APPLICATION_TYPE = 2 (competing continuation / competing renewal) whose BUDGET_START is strictly after the initial PROJECT_START and no later than initial PROJECT_START + 6 years; y = 0 if no such record exists and the cohort's full 6-year window is observed in the data cutoff. Rows whose window is not fully observed are dropped, never labeled 0.
task.usefulness: The binary outcome is not stored in any field: it requires reconstructing project continuity across annual support-year records and award types. It is uncommon rather than balanced: in the previously constructed FY2008-FY2017 release roughly 4,300 of 39,875 first-year R01 rows (about one in nine) received a competing renewal inside six years, so a constant negative baseline already reaches about 89 percent accuracy and the signal must be read from ranking and calibration metrics. The outcome still varies across institutes, review panels, organizations and investigator experience, so a model must beat fiscal-year cohort base rates and institutional identity baselines using only award-time metadata, and it must avoid the documented contamination channel in which PROJECT_END is extended on renewal.

title: Will a newly awarded NIH R01 project be continued through a competing renewal? Predicting federal research-funding continuation from award-time attributes
